title: Darcy-Weisbach Equation

f.description: Darcy-Weisbach friction factor (from Moody diagram or Colebrook-White)

applicability: Universal — valid for all fluids, all flow regimes. Preferred over Hazen-Williams for precision work.

title: Colebrook-White Equation (Friction Factor)
applicability: Implicit — requires iteration. Valid for turbulent flow (Re > 4000). For explicit approximation, use Swamee-Jain.

title: Swamee-Jain Explicit Friction Factor
applicability: Explicit approximation of Colebrook-White. Accurate to ±1% for 10⁻⁶ < ε/D < 10⁻² and 5000 < Re < 10⁸.

title: Hazen-Williams Equation
applicability: Empirical — only for water near 15°C, turbulent flow. US customary form: hf = (4.73 × L × Q^1.852) / (C^1.852 × D^4.87) with Q in cfs, D in ft.

title: Minor (Local) Loss
applicability: K values from tables/handbooks. For transitions between different diameters, use the higher velocity. Total minor loss = Σ(Ki × Vi²/(2g)).

title: Joukowsky Water Hammer Pressure

ΔH.description: Pressure surge head (above or below steady-state HGL)

ΔV.description: Change in velocity (positive for closure, negative for opening)

applicability: For instantaneous or rapid closure (tc < 2L/a). ΔP = ρ × a × ΔV (in pressure units). Example: a = 1000 m/s, ΔV = 2 m/s → ΔH = 204 m (2000 kPa surge).

K.description: Bulk modulus of water (2.2 GPa at 20°C)

E.description: Modulus of elasticity of pipe material

c₁.description: Pipe restraint factor (1.0 thin-wall anchored, 1-ν² thick-wall)

title: Critical Period (Wave Reflection Time)

Tcr.description: Critical time — round-trip wave travel time

applicability: Valve closure in time < Tcr produces full Joukowsky pressure. Closure time > 5×Tcr considered slow (significant attenuation).

title: System Head Curve (Pumped System)
equation: H_system = H_static + hf(Q) + hm(Q) = H_static + [f×L/(D×2g) + ΣK/(2g)] × (Q/A)²

H_system.description: Total dynamic head required at flow Q

applicability: Operating point = intersection of system curve and pump curve. For gravity systems, available head = H_static and flow is where friction + minor losses = H_static.

title: Economic Pipe Diameter (Bresse Formula)

K_b.description: Bresse coefficient (1.0–1.5 depending on cost assumptions)

applicability: Quick estimate. Results in velocity ≈ 0.9–1.5 m/s for K_b = 1.0–1.3. True economic diameter requires life-cycle cost analysis comparing capital cost vs. pumping energy cost.

title: Reynolds Number

ν.description: Kinematic viscosity of water (1.0×10⁻⁶ m²/s at 20°C)

applicability: Re < 2000: laminar. 2000–4000: transitional. > 4000: turbulent. Most water pipelines: Re > 10⁵ (fully turbulent).

title: Surge Tank Oscillation Period

T.description: Period of mass oscillation in surge tank

L.description: Length of pipeline between reservoir and surge tank

applicability: Simple surge tank (no throttling). Maximum upsurge: Z_max ≈ V₀ × √(L×At/(g×As)) where V₀ = initial steady-state velocity. Thoma criterion for stability: As_min = f×L×At/(2g×H_net) where H_net = net head.
